gap.consequence: A plugin cannot add a per-Arc-workspace navigation button/menu through current registered host surface, despite supported chat-tab actions.

minimalFollowupDesign: Under the same existing task after current browser repair, add one narrow render seam for workspace-level navigation actions, with a distinct typed layout-workspace identity rather than aliasing right-panel context.
Register its slot/context through existing manifest validation, activation and ExtensionSlot; keep one PluginHost and existing capability/disabled/error handling.

Any layout-changing command must use host-owned invocation checks and close protection, invalidate on connection/view/layout revocation, and never expose editable layout or business draft stores to plugins.
Place extension buttons beside rather than inside role=tab buttons; preserve roving-tab keyboard behavior and compact row height.
Keep current UI bounds 8 workspace tabs, 3 visible panes, 32 open views; do not silently widen them for plugin contributions.
acceptance: A real sample button/menu appears for the intended Arc workspace, triggers existing host authority, and disappears on disable/unregister.
Inactive/closed workspace or revoked connection cannot commit a delayed action; plugin dispose/activation failure produces bounded diagnostics.
Keyboard navigation, close-confirmation ownership, no nested interactive tab, both themes and narrow viewport remain covered.
Adding this slot does not require a second task progress record or revalidate unrelated green server PG tests.
performanceNote: AppLayoutPort currently serializes bounded layout identity; this audit did not measure cost and does not justify an optimization claim or rewrite. Future measurements should target meaningful render/subscription overhead on 3 visible and 32 retained views.
